{{Icelandic name|Einar}}
'''Einar Steingrímsson''' (born 20 July 1955<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-03-26 |title=Rektorsslagurinn 2015: Kynning á frambjóðendum |url=https://studentabladid.is/efni/2015/3/23/rektorsslagurinn2015 |access-date=2025-06-17 |website=Stúdentablaðið |language=en-US}}</ref>) is an Icelandic mathematician whose research lies in [[enumerative combinatorics]], especially the study of [[permutation pattern]]s and [[permutation statistics]]. He is a research professor (emeritus) in the School of Mathematics and Statistics at the [[University of Strathclyde]].<ref name="ECAinterview">{{cite journal |last=Mansour |first=Toufik |author-link=Toufik Mansour |year=2023 |title=Interview with Einar Steingrímsson |journal=Enumerative Combinatorics and Applications |volume=3 |issue=1 |pages=8 pp |doi=10.54550/ECA2023V3S1I2 |id=S3 I2|doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Einar grew up in Reykjavík and left secondary school early at age eighteen (the normal graduation age at the time was twenty), and trained as a ship builder at Slippstöðin in [[Akureyri]].<ref name=ECAinterview/> After completing qualifying examinations independently, he enrolled at the [[University of Pennsylvania]]. He graduated there as a BA and MA in mathematics in 1987, and as PhD at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1992 under the supervision of [[Richard P. Stanley]]; his dissertation was titled ''Permutation Statistics of Indexed and Poset Permutations''.<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Steingrímsson |first=Einar |title=Permutations statistics of indexed and poset permutations |date=1992 |degree=Ph.D. |publisher=Massachusetts Institute of Technology |hdl=1721.1/35952 |url=https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/35952}}</ref>

==Career==
Einar moved to [[Gothenburg]], Sweden, in 1990, while still a graduate student at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, and, in 1992, Einar was hired at [[Chalmers University of Technology]] as part of the joint mathematics institute with the [[University of Gothenburg]].<ref name="ECAhistory">{{cite journal |last=Steingrímsson |first=Einar |year=2023 |title=The History of the Gothenburg–Reykjavík–Strathclyde Combinatorics Group |journal=Enumerative Combinatorics and Applications |volume=3 |issue=1 |pages=9 pp |doi=10.54550/ECA2023V3S1H1 |id=S3 H1|doi-access=free }}</ref> In 2004 he became a professor of mathematics at [[Reykjavik University]]. From 2010 to 2021 he was a professor at the [[University of Strathclyde]] in Glasgow, Scotland.<ref name=ECAinterview/>

==Research==
Einar's research focuses on permutation statistics, pattern avoidance, and related enumerative problems.

* In a 1994 paper, he studied permutation statistics defined on colored permutations (then called indexed permutations), relating them to classical statistics such as descents and inversions.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Steingrı́msson |first=Einar |date=1994 |title=Permutation Statistics of Indexed Permutations |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0195669884710213 |journal=European Journal of Combinatorics |language=en |volume=15 |issue=2 |pages=187–205 |doi=10.1006/eujc.1994.1021|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

* In a 2000 paper joint with Eric Babson, he introduced vincular permutation patterns (then called "generalized patterns"); that paper also classified Mahonian statistics expressible via these patterns.<ref name="Babson2000">{{cite journal |last1=Babson |first1=Eric |last2=Steingrímsson |first2=Einar |year=2000 |title=Generalized permutation patterns and a classification of the Mahonian statistics |journal=Séminaire Lotharingien de Combinatoire |volume=44 |pages=Article B44b, 18 pp}}</ref>

* New Euler–Mahonian bi-statistics on permutations and words were described in a joint work with R. J. Clarke and Jiang Zeng, extending earlier Eulerian–Mahonian results.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Clarke |first1=Robert J |last2=Steingrı́msson |first2=Einar |last3=Zeng |first3=Jiang |date=1997 |title=New Euler–Mahonian Statistics on Permutations and Words |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0196885896905060 |journal=Advances in Applied Mathematics |language=en |volume=18 |issue=3 |pages=237–270 |doi=10.1006/aama.1996.0506|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

* Connections between permutation tableaux and pattern avoidance were examined in his joint work with [[Lauren Williams (mathematician)|Lauren K. Williams]], linking tableaux combinatorics to steady-state distributions in the asymmetric simple exclusion process.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Steingrímsson |first1=Einar |last2=Williams |first2=Lauren K. |author2-link=Lauren Williams (mathematician) |date=2007 |title=Permutation tableaux and permutation patterns |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0097316506000525 |journal=Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A |language=en |volume=114 |issue=2 |pages=211–234 |doi=10.1016/j.jcta.2006.04.001|arxiv=math/0507149 }}</ref>
* His joint work with Anders Claesson and Vít Jelínek established that the [[Stanley–Wilf conjecture#Allowable growth rates|growth rate]] of the class of 1324-avoiding permutations is at most 16, and presented a still-open conjecture that if true would lower this bound to <math>e^{\pi\sqrt{2/3}}</math>, approximately 13.00195.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Claesson |first1=Anders |last2=Jelínek |first2=Vít |last3=Steingrímsson |first3=Einar |date=2012 |title=Upper bounds for the Stanley–Wilf limit of 1324 and other layered patterns |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0097316512000891 |journal=Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A |language=en |volume=119 |issue=8 |pages=1680–1691 |doi=10.1016/j.jcta.2012.05.006|arxiv=1111.5736 }}</ref>
